title: Present a study's aim, method, or conclusion
subtitle: Rhetorical Synthesis · 37 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **37 of the official questions in Rhetorical Synthesis are this one** — 0 Easy, 23 Medium, 14 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The notes follow a research story: background or gap, who did the study, what they did, what they found, and what they concluded.
- The goal names ONE stage: 'emphasize the aim', 'present the conclusion', 'present the study and its findings', or a recommendation that came out of it.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Match the goal word to a stage: aim means purpose or question ('sought to', 'investigated whether'), findings or conclusion means result ('found', 'concluded', 'determined'), and a recommendation means advice.
- 2) Pick the choice built around that stage's content.
- For 'study and findings', the choice has to name the study AND its result.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: Choices describe the wrong stage of the same study.
When the goal asks for the aim, the trap reports the result.
When it asks for the conclusion, the trap describes the method or the background debate.
When the goal says 'study and its findings', the trap gives only one of the two.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
Choices describe the wrong stage of the same study.
When the goal asks for the aim, the trap reports the result.
